ProgramName: Master of Accounting
Requirements: Applicants to the Smeal One-Year MAcc Program must have an undergraduate degree from an accredited institution. Before starting the program in the fall, students must have completed all the prerequisites listed below. Students must also have a minimum grade of C for each course. Prerequisites include: Financial Accounting, Managerial Accounting, Intermediate Accounting I, Intermediate Accounting II, Cost Accounting, Introduction to Taxation, and Auditing. Non-native English speakers must also provide proof of English proficiency.
Description: The Penn State Smeal Master of Accounting (MAcc) Program offers two paths to a graduate degree and the 150 credit hours required to be a CPA: The Integrated MAcc Program and the One-Year MAcc Program. The program provides the specialized knowledge and professional skills needed for success in the accounting profession, preparing students for the challenges of the profession and meeting the requirements for CPA licensure in most states. Smeal accounting graduates are highly sought after by top accounting firms and corporations, gaining technical knowledge necessary for success in public accounting, corporate accounting, and other related fields.
Accredidation: Smeal is among the few business schools to be accredited by AACSB in both business and accounting.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Accounting Analytics
Requirements: The admission process for the program includes a completed online application, a current resume, a professional statement, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, GMAT or GRE scores (waivers available for qualified applicants), and two letters of recommendation.
Department: Penn State Smeal College of Business
Description: The Penn State Smeal College of Business is merging its two one-year accounting master’s programs — the Master of Science in Accounting Analytics (MAA) and the Master of Accounting (MAcc) — to create a single, comprehensive program: the Master of Science in Accounting Analytics. Starting in fall 2024, the new MAA curriculum will integrate coursework focused on data analytics and technology skills with traditional accounting courses. The curriculum is designed to equip students with the necessary skills to navigate the evolving landscape of the accounting profession and meet the increasing demand for professionals with expertise in data-driven decision-making. The program will offer one-year master’s students two paths to CPA licensure: a non-business path for students with a non-accounting background and an accounting path for those with a bachelor’s degree in accounting. As part of the program, students will participate in a three-credit immersion experience, working in teams to address a real-world accounting analytics problem. They also will gain exposure to emerging technologies like blockchain, artificial intelligence and robotic process automation. The MAA program is STEM-designated and prepares students for the CPA exam.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Acoustics
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Undergraduate background in physics, engineering, or mathematics, including at least two semesters of calculus-based physics and mathematics through differential equations, is required. A minimum junior/senior grade-point average of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale) is required. GRE scores are not required for admission.
Description: The Intercollege Graduate Degree Program (IGDP) in Acoustics is an interdisciplinary program that leads to the Master of Engineering (M.Eng.), Master of Science (M.S.), and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees. The program is supported by various University departments, including Aerospace Engineering, Architectural Engineering, Bioengineering, Electrical Engineering, Engineering Science and Mechanics, Mechanical Engineering, Oceanography, and Physics. The program offers a broad-based curriculum in acoustics, which includes courses in physical acoustics, underwater acoustics, signal processing, transducer design, noise and vibration control, architectural acoustics, and bio-acoustics. Students are required to take a core of courses in physical acoustics and mathematics, followed by more specialized courses in their areas of interest.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Acoustics
Requirements: For admission to the Graduate Program in Acoustics, an applicant must have a baccalaureate degree in engineering, physics, mathematics, or a closely related field from an accredited institution. Students with a senior-year grade-point average of 3.0 or higher (on a 4.0 scale) and appropriate course backgrounds will be considered for admission. Official transcripts, a statement of objectives, and three letters of recommendation are required. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission.
Description: The Graduate Program in Acoustics is a unique interdisciplinary program that leads to the Master of Engineering (M.Eng.), Master of Science (M.S.), and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degrees. The Acoustics Program is the only program in the United States that offers the Ph.D. in Acoustics. Research and coursework are offered in several areas: Physical Acoustics; Structural Acoustics and Vibration; Underwater Acoustics; Aeroacoustics and Propeller Noise; Audio Engineering and Signal Processing; Architectural Acoustics; Nonlinear Acoustics; Medical and Biological Ultrasound; Psychological and Physiological Acoustics; Outdoor Sound Propagation; and Computational Acoustics. The Graduate Program in Acoustics is an intercollege graduate degree program. The program is broad in scope and provides students with a thorough foundation in the fundamental principles of acoustics.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Additive Manufacturing and Design
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree in engineering, science, or a related field from an accredited institution with a minimum GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale). Application requirements include official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, a statement of career and educational goals (one to two pages), a resume or curriculum vitae, and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required.
Description: The Additive Manufacturing and Design (AMD) program is a first-of-its-kind multidisciplinary program that provides students with a unique opportunity to learn the fundamentals of additive manufacturing (AM) and to apply these principles to the design of components and systems. The Master of Science (M.S.) in Additive Manufacturing and Design degree is a 30-credit residential program for students interested in a research-based experience and for those who wish to pursue a doctoral degree. Students work with world-class faculty on cutting-edge research in additive manufacturing.

ProgramName: Master of Engineering in Additive Manufacturing and Design
Requirements: Admission requirements for the Master of Engineering in Additive Manufacturing and Design include: official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, a statement of intent (outlining professional goals and reasons for applying), a current resume, and three letters of reference. International students must also submit scores from the TOEFL or the IELTS. For admission to the Graduate School, an applicant must hold either (1) a baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution or (2) a tertiary (postsecondary) degree that is deemed comparable to a four-year bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited institution.
Description: The Additive Manufacturing and Design (AMD) graduate program at Penn State provides students with the opportunity to study the latest in 3D printing technology and its applications. The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) in Additive Manufacturing and Design is a 30-credit degree program designed for professionals and students who want to build their expertise in the field of additive manufacturing. The program provides a unique opportunity for students to learn about the entire AM process, from design to production, and gain hands-on experience with the latest AM technologies. Students integrate graduate-level coursework across multiple departments including mechanical engineering, industrial engineering, engineering science and mechanics, and materials science and engineering to provide a holistic view of the AM industry. All students in the M.Eng. degree program must complete a capstone project (3 credits) as their culminating experience, which provides the opportunity to apply the knowledge and skills they have gained throughout the program to a real-world AM problem.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for admission, applicants must have a bachelor’s degree in engineering, physical sciences, or mathematics from an accredited institution. A minimum grade-point average of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale) for the junior and senior years is required. Applicants must submit transcripts, a statement of intent, a resume, and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required for admission to our graduate programs.
Description: The Department of Aerospace Engineering offers Master of Science and Doctor of Philosophy degrees. Graduate study and research are conducted in a wide variety of specialist areas, including: aeroacoustics, aerodynamics, aeroelasticity, air-breathing and rocket propulsion, astrodynamics, autonomous systems, composites and lightweight structures, computational fluid dynamics, control systems, flight mechanics, fluid mechanics, rotorcraft, smart structures, space logistics, space propulsion, and wind energy. The Master of Science (M.S.) degree program is designed for students to gain advanced knowledge in aerospace engineering. The M.S. degree is a research-oriented degree that requires a thesis.

In addition to the Graduate School application, the department requires: official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, a statement of purpose, a resume or curriculum vitae, and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required for admission to the Aerospace Engineering graduate program.
Description: The graduate program in Aerospace Engineering is designed to provide students with the opportunity to develop a higher level of knowledge in aerospace engineering and to prepare them for careers in the aerospace industry. The M.Eng. degree is a non-thesis professional master's degree. Graduate study in aerospace engineering at Penn State is a multifaceted activity, and it involves many people and facilities from throughout the University. Graduate students come to Penn State with diverse backgrounds and interests, and they find a wide range of courses and research opportunities from which to choose. Students can study and conduct research in several areas of aerospace engineering, including: aerodynamics and fluid dynamics; aerospace structures and materials; flight dynamics and control; rotorcraft; and space systems.

Requirements: Admission to the Ph.D. program is based on a student’s performance in his/her previous academic work and his/her potential for advanced study and research. Qualified students with B.S. or M.S. degrees in aerospace engineering or related fields can apply for admission. GRE scores are required for all applicants. There is no minimum score for admission. Requirements for admission to the Ph.D. program include: a minimum grade point average (GPA) of 3.3/4.0 in a master’s degree program or 3.5/4.0 in a baccalaureate program.
Description: Aerospace Engineering graduate programs are intended to provide students with a deep understanding of the fundamental principles of aerospace engineering and to develop their research and design capabilities. The programs cover a wide range of topics, including aerodynamics, propulsion, structures and materials, dynamics and control, and space systems. Students have the opportunity to participate in cutting-edge research in these areas, and to work with world-renowned faculty and researchers. The Ph.D. program is designed for students who are interested in pursuing a career in research and development in academia, industry, or government.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in African American and Diaspora Studies
Requirements: The program requires a minimum junior/senior grade-point average of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale). Applicants must submit a statement of purpose, a CV or resume, a writing sample, and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required for admission.
Description: The M.A. program in African American and Diaspora Studies is a multidisciplinary program that provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the history, culture, and experiences of people of African descent in the United States and throughout the African Diaspora. The program is designed to prepare students for doctoral study in African American Studies or related fields, as well as for careers in education, public service, non-governmental organizations, and the private sector.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Agricultural and Biological Engineering
Requirements: To be considered for admission, applicants should have a B.S. degree in a related engineering field. Non-engineering students may be admitted, but may be required to complete additional engineering course work as a deficiency. Admission is based on a combination of undergraduate GPA, letters of recommendation, statement of purpose, and relevant experience. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) is expected. Requirements include a completed Graduate School application, transcripts from all institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, a one-to-two page Statement of Purpose, and a CV/resume. GRE scores are not required.
Department: College of Agricultural Sciences and College of Engineering
Description: The graduate program in Agricultural and Biological Engineering (ABE) is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge to address the grand challenges of the 21st century in the areas of food, water, energy, and the environment. Students in the program have the opportunity to conduct research in areas such as bioproducts and biosystems engineering, food and bioprocess engineering, and natural resource engineering. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research, development, and professional practice in the biological, food, and environmental sectors. The M.S. degree is a research-oriented degree that requires a thesis.

Description: The Agricultural and Biological Engineering (A B E) graduate program is a research-oriented program that provides students with the opportunity to pursue advanced study and research in the application of engineering principles to biological and agricultural systems. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research, teaching, and industry. Current research areas in the department include: bioprocessing and biofuels; precision health; machine systems and agricultural safety; natural resource engineering; and food engineering. The Ph.D. program is designed to provide students with the opportunity to pursue advanced study and research in the application of engineering principles to biological and agricultural systems. Candidates must demonstrate high-level scholarly achievement and ability to perform independent research. The program consists of a combination of course work and research that is tailored to the student's interests and needs.

Applicants should have a B.S. degree in a biological or agricultural science with at least a 3.00 grade-point average (on a 4.00 scale) for the last two years of undergraduate study.
Description: The graduate program in Agricultural and Environmental Plant Science (AEPS) provides students with a broad background in plant science and related disciplines, and provides specialized training in a specific area of interest. The program is flexible and can be tailored to meet the needs of students with a variety of career goals. Students may choose to specialize in areas such as: agronomy, horticulture, plant breeding, plant physiology, plant molecular biology, weed science, and turfgrass science.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Agricultural and Environmental Plant Science
Requirements: Admission to the AEPS graduate program is based on a review of the following information: Statement of Purpose (not to exceed two pages); Resume or Curriculum Vitae; Official Transcripts; Three letters of recommendation; and TOEFL/IELTS scores (international students only). The GRE is not required for admission to the AEPS graduate program. While there is no minimum GPA requirement, most successful applicants have a GPA of 3.0 or higher. Students should have a B.S. or M.S. degree in a related field.
Description: The Agricultural and Environmental Plant Science (AEPS) graduate program in the Department of Plant Science offers a unique opportunity for students to tailor their studies according to their interests and professional goals. Through its focus on plant and soil science, the AEPS program offers a high-quality education and diverse research opportunities for students to investigate the fundamental and applied aspects of plant-based systems in agriculture and the environment. Faculty research spans from the molecular to the landscape scale, including plant molecular biology, genomics, and physiology; plant health; crop science; horticultural science; soil science; and agroecology. Students may work in various environments, including state-of-the-art laboratories and greenhouses, research farms, and field sites throughout the region and the world. The AEPS program is designed to prepare graduates for successful careers in academia, industry, government, and non-governmental organizations.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in American Studies
Requirements: Applicants must submit: a statement of intent, a writing sample, three letters of recommendation, a resume or curriculum vitae, and official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission.
Concentration: Museum Studies and Public Heritage; Doctoral Studies
Description: The M.A. program in American Studies is designed for students whose career goals or current positions can be enhanced by the study of American culture and society. In the course of their work, students are encouraged to consider the diversity of the American experience, the importance of historical context, and the relationship of the United States to the rest of the world. Because American Studies is an interdisciplinary field, students can pursue their interests across a wide range of subjects. Some students concentrate on history, literature, or the arts, while others emphasize folklore, museum studies, or public history. The program is particularly strong in the study of regional culture, popular culture, and the social history of ordinary people.
ScholarshipType: Graduate Assistantships, Fellowships (American Studies Graduate Fellowship)

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in American Studies
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Ph.D. program, an applicant must have a Master’s degree in American Studies or a related field (e.g., history, literature, communications, art history, sociology, anthropology, etc.). For admission, an applicant should have a minimum grade-point average of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale). Applicants must submit official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, three letters of recommendation from persons who can evaluate the applicant’s academic potential, a statement of intent (approximately 500 words) outlining the student’s preparation for graduate study, why they wish to pursue the Ph.D. in American Studies at Penn State Harrisburg, and their specific research interests, a sample of the student’s academic writing (e.g., a chapter from a Master’s thesis or a major seminar paper) that demonstrates the student’s ability to conduct original research and to write clearly and analytically, and a resume or curriculum vitae. GRE scores are not required for admission to the Ph.D. program in American Studies.
Description: The Ph.D. in American Studies program at Penn State Harrisburg is the only one of its kind in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania. This program is designed for students who want to pursue advanced research and teaching in the field of American Studies. It provides a comprehensive foundation in the methods and theories of American Studies and allows students to develop specialized expertise in particular areas of American culture and history. Students in the program work closely with faculty mentors to develop their research projects and gain teaching experience. The program is ideal for those who wish to pursue careers in academia, museums, government, or the private sector.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Anatomy
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. A junior/senior grade-point average of 3.0 or higher is required. Prerequisites include: two semesters of biology, two semesters of chemistry, and two semesters of physics. Scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) are not required for admission. Application requirements include a personal statement, resume/CV, three letters of recommendation, and official transcripts.
Description: The M.S. program in Anatomy is designed to provide students with a comprehensive background in the anatomical sciences (gross anatomy, histology, embryology, and neuroanatomy) and to provide experience in research. The program is intended for students who wish to pursue a career in research or teaching in the anatomical sciences.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Anatomy
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Desired coursework includes biology, general chemistry, organic chemistry, physics and calculus. Applicants should have a minimum GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale). Required application materials include a resume/curriculum vitae, a personal statement (should include a brief description of your professional and/or research experiences, your career goals, and why you are interested in the Anatomy PhD program), three letters of recommendation, and official transcripts. Description: The Anatomy PhD program at Penn State College of Medicine is a research-intensive program that trains students to become independent research scientists and educators in the anatomical sciences. The program's primary objective is to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the anatomical sciences (including gross anatomy, embryology, histology and neurobiology) and the skills needed to conduct high-quality research. Our program is unique in its focus on preparing students for careers in academic medicine, where they will be expected to excel in both research and teaching.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Animal Science
Requirements: Applicants apply for admission through the J. Jeffrey and Ann Marie Fox Graduate School. To be considered for admission, applicants must have: 1. A baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited institution (or international equivalent). 2. A minimum grade-point average of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale). 3. Three letters of recommendation. 4. A curriculum vitae or resume. 5. A statement of interests. 6. Identification of a member of the Animal Science Graduate Faculty who has agreed to serve as the applicant’s graduate adviser.
Concentration: animal management, growth and developmental biology, nutrition, physiology, and production systems
Description: The Animal Science graduate program offers two degrees: Master of Science (M.S.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.). Program objectives are to provide students with the necessary education and research experience to become leaders in the animal science industry, higher education, and government. These objectives are achieved through a combination of required and elective coursework and the research experience. Graduate study in Animal Science is organized into five areas of specialization: animal management, growth and developmental biology, nutrition, physiology, and production systems. Each student's program is tailored to the individual's interests and needs.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Animal Science
Requirements: To be considered for admission to the Animal Science graduate program, an applicant must have a B.S., B.A., or equivalent degree from an accredited institution. A minimum grade-point average of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale) for the last two years of undergraduate study or for a master's degree is required. Application materials must include official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, a curriculum vitae or resume, and a personal statement (statement of intent) describing professional goals and reasons for applying. GRE scores are not required.
Concentration: breeding and genomics, nutrition, physiology, and production systems
Description: The Department of Animal Science offers M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in Animal Science. The goal of the program is to provide students with the opportunity to gain advanced knowledge in the fields of animal breeding and genomics, nutrition, physiology, and production systems. Students will develop research skills and the ability to critically analyze scientific literature, communicate effectively, and conduct independent research.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Anthropology
Requirements: Applicants should have a junior/senior grade-point average of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale) and must submit results of the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) (verbal, quantitative, and analytical writing). Three letters of recommendation and a sample of scholarly writing must be submitted. The deadline for applications is December 1st for the following fall.
Concentration: Evolutionary Anthropology, Integrative Anthropology
Description: The Department of Anthropology provides students with a high degree of flexibility in choosing their own areas of study. At the same time, we ensure that our students receive a thorough grounding in the essentials of anthropological theory and research methods. Graduate students in the department choose one of two program tracks: 1. Evolutionary Anthropology or 2. Integrative Anthropology. The Department of Anthropology does not admit students for a terminal M.A. degree. The M.A. is awarded only to students who have been admitted to the Ph.D. program and who have completed the M.A. requirements on the way to the Ph.D.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Anthropology
Requirements: Applicants must provide official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with the applicant's academic performance, a statement of purpose (approximately 2-3 pages) describing research interests and professional goals, a resume or curriculum vitae, and a writing sample (such as a published article, a chapter from a master's thesis, or a term paper). The Department of Anthropology does not require the GRE for admission and these scores will not be reviewed.
Concentration: Archaeology, Biological Anthropology, and Cultural Anthropology
Description: The Department of Anthropology graduate program offers M.A. and Ph.D. degrees. It is a research-oriented program, with three major areas of concentration: archaeology, biological anthropology, and cultural anthropology. The department’s focus is on the signature strategic theme of “Integrative Graduate Training in Human-Environment Systems,” which spans all three concentrations and emphasizes the study of humans as biological and cultural organisms that both shape and are shaped by their environments. Graduate students are encouraged to develop a broad background in anthropology as well as specialized expertise in their chosen area of study. Student Learning Outcomes: Demonstrate mastery of the student’s specific research area and more general mastery of the subfield (archaeology, biological anthropology, or cultural anthropology); Identify and master the methodologies of their subfield (archaeology, biological anthropology, or cultural anthropology); Identify relevant research questions and conduct independent research that addresses these questions and makes a contribution to the field of anthropology; Communicate research findings in the form of a doctoral dissertation, and in papers presented at professional meetings and published in peer-reviewed journals; Be able to teach anthropology at the university level.

ProgramName: Master of Education in Applied Behavior Analysis
Requirements: In addition to the University graduate admission requirements, applicants must provide: Evidence of an earned bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. Two letters of recommendation. A resume. A personal statement (max 500 words) describing the applicant's experience and interests in the field of applied behavior analysis and how the program aligns with their professional goals. An interview may be required.
Description: The Master of Education in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) program is designed for students who are interested in working with individuals with autism spectrum disorders, intellectual and developmental disabilities, and other behavioral challenges. Applied behavior analysis is a scientific approach to understanding behavior and how it is affected by the environment. This program provides students with the knowledge and skills necessary to design, implement, and evaluate effective behavioral interventions.

Description: The Ph.D. program is designed for students whose goal is a career in university teaching or research, or museum curating. Students have access to a variety of state-of-the-art facilities for research, including the Genomics, Proteomics, Metabolomics, and Microscopy core facilities. Biological Engineering is a broad-based curriculum that provides students with the opportunity to pursue a wide range of interests. Students may choose to specialize in the following areas: bioprocess engineering, biological systems engineering, biomass energy, food engineering, and machine systems. The program consists of core courses in biological engineering, plus courses in other engineering disciplines, the biological sciences, and the physical sciences. Research is a major component of the graduate program. Opportunities exist for research in many different areas, including: agricultural and biological systems, bioenergy, food and bioprocessing, and natural resources.

Students must apply through the J. Jeffrey and Ann Marie Fox Graduate School. ProgramName: Master of Science in Chemical Engineering

Description: The Intercollege Graduate Degree Program in Ecology is a broadly based graduate program, providing students with the opportunity to pursue a diversity of research interests in the field of ecology. The curriculum is designed to be flexible, allowing students to tailor their course of study to meet their individual research interests and career goals. The M.S. program is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in ecology and to prepare them for careers in research, management, or teaching, or for further graduate study.

This brings together a wide diversity of expertise in the ecology of animals, plants, and microorganisms from molecular and physiological ecology to population, community, and ecosystem levels and on through to landscape, global, and applied ecology. The primary goal of the Ecology Program is to provide a broad-based, interdisciplinary graduate education in ecology. Students have the opportunity to work with faculty members from multiple departments and colleges, which allows for a unique perspective on ecological research.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Economics
Requirements: The department does not offer a terminal Master's degree. Only those students who intend to work toward the Ph.D. degree are admitted to the graduate program. To apply, the applicant should provide the following: The Graduate School application and application fee; A Statement of Purpose; Transcripts from all institutions attended; Three letters of recommendation; GRE scores; TOEFL or IELTS scores (if applicable). Applicants should have a strong background in economics (including microeconomic and macroeconomic theory and statistics) and mathematics (including one year of calculus).
Description: The graduate program in economics at Penn State is designed for students interested in obtaining a Ph.D. in economics. The program is centered on the University Park campus, which is the largest of Penn State’s campuses and is home to most of the University’s research and graduate programs. The primary goal of the program is to provide students with the skills they need to conduct original research in economics. The first year of the program is devoted to core courses in microeconomic theory, macroeconomic theory, and econometrics. In the second year, students begin to specialize in one or more of the department’s many fields of strength, which include: econometrics, industrial organization, international economics, macroeconomics, microeconomic theory, and development economics. Students also begin to work on their own research projects in the second year, often in collaboration with faculty members. The M.A. degree in economics is only available to students who are already enrolled in the Ph.D. program. The M.A. degree may be awarded as an interim degree for students in the Ph.D. program or if the student terminates study before completing the Ph.D. requirements.

Requirements: The following documents are required for an application to be considered complete: Official Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores (The GRE is optional for applicants). Have scores sent to Penn State (Code 2660). A brief (two- to three-page) statement of purpose describing the applicant's research interests and career goals. International applicants should also see the Graduate School’s requirements for international students, which includes information on demonstrating English language proficiency (TOEFL/IELTS).

Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree in Educational Theory and Policy is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching in the fields of educational policy, history of education, philosophy of education, and sociology of education. The program provides students with a strong foundation in these fields and allows them to specialize in an area of interest. The Ph.D. program in Educational Theory and Policy (EDTHP) provides students with an opportunity to engage in advanced study and research in the social and philosophical foundations of education and educational policy. The program is designed to develop the students' ability to conduct independent research and to prepare them for leadership roles in higher education, research organizations, and government agencies.
ScholarshipType: Graduate Assistantships, Fellowships, and Merit-based Scholarships

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Education Policy and Leadership (Emphasis in Educational Leadership)
Requirements: Applicants should have a junior/senior grade-point average of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale). Students must provide: a statement of purpose that describes the applicant’s professional goals, research interests, and why the applicant is interested in the program; letters of recommendation from three people who are best qualified to evaluate the applicant's ability to succeed in graduate study; a curriculum vitae or resume; and one writing sample that demonstrates the applicant’s ability to write at the graduate level. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required for admission.
Concentration: Educational Leadership
Description: The College of Education at Penn State is launching a unified doctoral program beginning in the fall 2024 semester. The doctor of philosophy (Ph.D.) in Education Policy and Leadership (EDPL) will bring together three existing programs — Educational Leadership, Higher Education, and Education Theory and Policy — as emphasis areas within a single degree. The new Ph.D. in Education Policy and Leadership is designed to provide students with a deep understanding of the complex challenges facing education systems today. The program will offer a core curriculum that covers foundational topics in education policy and leadership, as well as specialized coursework in each of the three emphasis areas. Students also will have the opportunity to engage in research with world-class faculty and gain practical experience through internships and other field-based learning opportunities.

Description: The Higher Education program is designed to provide students with a broad understanding of the field of higher education from a variety of disciplinary and professional perspectives. This degree program focuses on developing the research skills and knowledge necessary to conduct original research that contributes to the field of higher education. ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Educational Leadership
Requirements: Applicants are expected to have a grade-point average of 3.00 or higher (on a 4.00 scale) for the last two years of undergraduate study and a 3.50 or higher for graduate work. A master's degree in educational leadership or a related field is preferred but not required. Required application materials include official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, three letters of recommendation from professional and academic sources, an up-to-date resume or curriculum vitae, a statement of purpose (approximately 500-1000 words) indicating reasons for applying and research interests, and a writing sample (e.g., a published article, master's thesis, or course paper). For international applicants, scores from the TOEFL or IELTS are required. Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required for applicants applying for the Summer/Fall 2024 and 2025 admission cycles.
Description: The Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree program in Educational Leadership is designed for students who are interested in pursuing careers as researchers or faculty in higher education, as policy analysts or educational leaders at the state, national, or international levels. The Ph.D. degree requires students to complete a common set of core courses and provides students with considerable flexibility in selecting additional courses that align with their interests and career goals. Students in the program develop expertise in research design and data analysis that will allow them to contribute to the professional knowledge base in the field of educational leadership.

The requirement for GRE scores for Doctor of Education (D.Ed.) and Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) applications has been waived. Required application materials include: three letters of recommendation from professional colleagues or university faculty, a statement of interest (one-to-two pages) describing the applicant’s background and professional goals, a resume or curriculum vitae, a recent sample of professional writing, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, and TOEFL/IELTS scores for international students if applicable.
Description: Our Doctor of Education (D.Ed.) program in Educational Leadership is designed for students who are preparing for or currently holding leadership positions in K-12 schools, intermediate units, and state departments of education. The D.Ed. degree program is designed for mid-career professionals (e.g., teachers, principals, department heads, assistant superintendents, etc.) who are interested in pursuing a doctoral degree that will help them to improve their professional practice and to have a greater impact in the organizations they serve. The D.Ed. program is a professional degree, and as such, it focuses on the application of research and theory to the problems of practice.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Educational Psychology
Requirements: Application requirements for the Educational Psychology Graduate Program at Penn State include a completed Graduate School application and payment of the application fee, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, a statement of professional goals and research interests, a current resume or curriculum vitae, and a sample of scholarly writing (e.g., a thesis, a term paper, or a published article). GRE scores are not required for admission to this program.
Concentration: Learning and Development; Educational and Psychological Measurement, Evaluation, and Statistics
Description: The Educational Psychology program is designed for students who want to obtain a master's degree in Educational Psychology as an end in itself or as a step toward a doctoral degree. Students in the program may focus their study in one of two main areas: (1) Learning and Development or (2) Educational and Psychological Measurement, Evaluation, and Statistics. The program provides a broad background in educational psychology, including learning, development, and research methods.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Epidemiology
Requirements: Applicants must hold either (1) a baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution or (2) a post-baccalaureate graduate or professional degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution, or its equivalent from a foreign institution. A minimum grade-point average of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) is required. Application materials must include official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, a resume or curriculum vitae, a statement of purpose (personal statement) outlining goals and research interests, and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required for admission to this program.
Description: The Epidemiology PhD program provides students with the knowledge and skills to become independent researchers and leaders in the field of epidemiology. Students will learn to design and conduct epidemiologic studies, analyze complex data sets, and interpret and communicate research findings. The program emphasizes a multidisciplinary approach, with opportunities for collaboration with faculty and researchers across various departments and centers at Penn State. The Doctor of Philosophy in Epidemiology program is designed to provide advanced training in the concepts and methods of epidemiology. The program's goal is to prepare students for careers in research and teaching in academic, government and private-sector settings. The curriculum includes coursework in epidemiologic methods, biostatistics and several substantive areas of epidemiology. Students also receive training in the ethical conduct of research and in the communication of research findings. A key component of the program is the completion of a dissertation based on original research.

Students in the MGIS program have the opportunity to study a variety of topics, including GIS programming, remote sensing, spatial analysis, and project management. ProgramName: Master of Science in Marketing Analytics

Offered through the Penn State Smeal College of Business, this program provides a curriculum focused on the application of data analysis to marketing problems. Students can learn to use industry-standard tools to extract insights from complex data sets, develop predictive models, and communicate data-driven recommendations to leadership.
Accredidation: The Penn State Smeal College of Business is AACSB accredited.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Mass Communications

Description: Our Ph.D. program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching. Students work with a faculty of world-class scholars and researchers. Students in the mass communications Ph.D. program develop a strong foundation in theory and research methods, which they apply to their own research interests. The curriculum is designed to provide students with the skills they need to conduct original research and to teach at the university level. Requirements: Applicants apply for admission to the M.A. program in Media Studies through the Graduate School at Penn State. To be considered for admission, an applicant must have a baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited institution or the equivalent from a foreign institution. The language of instruction at Penn State is English. All international applicants must take and report scores for the TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language) or the IELTS (International English Language Testing System), with the exceptions noted in the Graduate School Admissions Requirements. Scores from the Graduate Record Examination (GRE) are not required for admission. Along with the online application, applicants must submit: Transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; Resume; Statement of purpose (approximately 500-1000 words); Three letters of recommendation; Writing sample (e.g., a research paper from a course).
Department: Donald P. Bellisario College of Communications
Description: The Media Studies M.A. program is a resident, research-oriented program that requires a thesis. Students take a core of required courses and then choose from a variety of electives that focus on the social and psychological effects of media, as well as media theory and various research methodologies. The program is designed for students who are preparing for doctoral studies or for research-related careers in the media or media-related industries. Research themes of the graduate faculty include: media effects, media theory, international communications, telecommunications, emerging media technologies, media law and policy, media history, critical and cultural studies, and strategic communications. Research facilities include the Media Effects Research Laboratory and the Media Research Group.

ProgramName: Master of Arts in Music
Requirements: Admission to the Master of Arts program is based on an audition (for the applied music track only) or on the evaluation of research papers and evidence of an adequate background in music history and music theory. Applicants must provide an application to the Graduate School, official transcripts, and three letters of recommendation. Specific track requirements include: for Musicology, two research papers on music subjects; for Music Theory, one or two analysis or research papers; for Applied Music, an audition is required. GRE scores are not required for any track.
Concentration: Musicology, Music Theory
Description: The master of arts (M.A.) in music is a research-oriented degree that provides students with the opportunity to pursue advanced study in musicology and music theory. The program is designed to prepare students for doctoral study and for careers in teaching, research, and other professional areas.
Accredidation: The School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Master of Education in Music Education
Requirements: Applicants must hold a bachelor’s degree in music education from an accredited institution or a baccalaureate degree in music with a teaching certificate. A minimum grade-point average of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) for the last two years of undergraduate study is required. Applicants must submit the official Graduate School application, transcripts, three letters of recommendation, a current resume, a statement of professional goals, and a writing sample (scholarly paper or essay).
Description: The Master of Music Education (M.M.E.) degree is a professional degree that is intended to help the music teacher refine their teaching, learn new techniques, and examine current research and its implications for the classroom. The M.M.E. is a 30-credit program that is typically completed during three consecutive summers. The curriculum includes courses in music education research, history, and philosophy, as well as pedagogy and music theory/history.
Accredidation: The School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Music Education
Requirements: To be considered for the Doctor of Philosophy degree, an applicant must have a master’s degree in music education or a related field from an accredited institution and at least three years of successful K-12 school music teaching experience. Application requirements include a formal letter of application stating your purpose in applying for graduate study, your professional goals, and your research interests; a current resume/CV; three letters of recommendation; and an example of scholarly writing (e.g., a master's thesis, a term paper, or a published article). An interview with the music education faculty is also required. The GRE is not required.
Description: The Ph.D. in Music Education is intended for individuals who have had successful experience teaching music in elementary or secondary schools and who wish to prepare for careers in higher education. The program is designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge to conduct research, to lead and teach in collegiate music education programs, and to contribute to the profession through scholarship and service. The program is highly individualized, allowing students to work closely with their faculty advisor to design a program of study that meets their specific needs and interests.
Accredidation: The School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Master of Music in Music Performance
Requirements: Admission is based on the student’s undergraduate record (all transcripts), three letters of recommendation from professional references, and a successful audition or an interview/audition. Admission to the M.M. degree program in Performance requires that the applicant demonstrate, through an audition, a high level of proficiency in his or her performing area. Candidates for the M.M. degree should have an undergraduate degree in music or music education or its equivalent.
Concentration: Music Performance
Description: The School of Music offers the Master of Arts, Master of Music, and Doctor of Philosophy degrees. The M.Mus. degree is a professional degree in music. Options include composition, conducting, music education, music performance, piano pedagogy and performance, and voice pedagogy and performance. Students in the M.Mus. degree program engage in advanced work in their area of specialization. In addition, students complete course work in music history and music theory. In the Music Performance option, students are required to complete a certain number of credits in their primary performance area, as well as pedagogy and literature courses. A solo recital is also required.
Accredidation: The graduate programs in music are accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Doctor of Musical Arts
Requirements: Admission to the D.M.A. program is based on a successful audition and interview, as well as the applicant's previous academic record. Applicants to the D.M.A. degree are required to complete an interview with the piano faculty and may be asked to present a short lecture on a pedagogical or performance-related topic of their choice. Audition requirements include a program of at least sixty minutes of music, representing at least three stylistic periods, including a complete sonata or other major work from the Classical period; a major work from the Romantic period; and a major work of the 20th or 21st century. All audition repertoire must be performed from memory.
Concentration: Piano Performance
Description: The Doctor of Musical Arts (D.M.A.) degree is the highest professional degree for musicians who wish to pursue a career in performance and/or teaching. The program is designed to provide students with the necessary skills and knowledge to succeed as professional musicians in a variety of settings. Students in the D.M.A. program in piano performance will have the opportunity to work with world-renowned faculty, participate in a variety of performance opportunities, and engage in research and scholarly activity. The program consists of a combination of coursework, performance requirements, and a final project. Coursework includes music theory, music history, and pedagogy, as well as specialized courses in piano literature and performance practice. Performance requirements include solo recitals, chamber music performances, and concerto performances. The final project consists of a written document and a public presentation or performance.
Accredidation: The School of Music is an accredited institutional member of the National Association of Schools of Music (NASM).

ProgramName: Master of Science in Neuroscience
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution and are expected to have a strong background in the biological and physical sciences. Admission is based on the applicant's academic record, letters of recommendation, and a statement of goals and interests. Application materials include official transcripts, three letters of recommendation, and a curriculum vitae or resume.
Description: The Neuroscience Graduate Program is an interdisciplinary program that provides students with a broad background in neuroscience as well as intensive training in a specialized area of research. To meet these goals, the curriculum includes a broad-based core course in neuroscience and a requirement for research rotations in different laboratories during the first year. In the second and subsequent years, students take more specialized elective courses and focus on their independent research project.

Description: The Neuroscience graduate program is an interdisciplinary program that provides students with broad exposure to the field of neuroscience while allowing for specialization in areas ranging from molecular and cellular neuroscience to systems and behavioral neuroscience. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching in academic, industrial, and governmental settings.

A minimum grade-point average of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale) for the last two years of undergraduate study is required. ProgramName: Master of Engineering in Nuclear Engineering
Requirements: Admission to the M.Eng. program in Nuclear Engineering requires a baccalaureate degree in engineering or the sciences. A minimum grade-point average of 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale) for the last two years of undergraduate study is required. Prerequisites for the program include mathematics through differential equations and a year of physics. Official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended and three letters of recommendation are also required.
Description: The Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) degree is a non-thesis professional degree that can be earned through the Penn State World Campus or in residence. This program is designed to provide students with the necessary background for a career in the nuclear industry or in a national laboratory. Nuclear engineering is a multi-disciplinary field with many types of career opportunities. Nuclear engineers can work on the development of nuclear power plants for large-scale electricity generation, or for propulsion of submarines, ships and spacecraft. Nuclear engineers also apply nuclear radiation and isotopes in medicine, such as in the diagnosis and treatment of cancer. They also apply these same techniques in industry for the inspection of materials and the development of new materials. Some nuclear engineers work on the development of nuclear-fusion-based power plants. Other nuclear engineers specialize in the nuclear fuel cycle, including the mining, processing and enrichment of uranium, the design and fabrication of nuclear fuel, the management of spent fuel, and the disposal of radioactive waste.

A minimum grade-point average of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) is required. Additional requirements include official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions, three professional references, a goal statement, a current resume or curriculum vitae, and a current license as a registered nurse. GRE scores are not required for admission.
Department: Ross and Carol Nese College of Nursing
Concentration: Adult Gerontology Acute Care Nurse Practitioner, Adult Gerontology Primary Care Nurse Practitioner, Family Nurse Practitioner, Leadership
Description: The Penn State Doctor of Nursing Practice (DNP) program is a professional doctoral degree that prepares nurses for the highest level of clinical nursing practice. The D.N.P. program focuses on the clinical aspects of nursing and provides nurses with the skills and knowledge to lead healthcare teams, influence healthcare policy, and implement evidence-based practices. The program is designed to prepare nurses as clinical experts and leaders in the field. Penn State offers two entry points for the DNP program: B.S.N. to D.N.P. and Post-Master's D.N.P.

Description: The Penn State Physician Assistant Program’s mission is to educate physician assistants to provide compassionate, high-quality, patient-centered care and to improve the health of the people and communities they serve. The 24-month, 101-credit program is designed to prepare students for the complexities of modern medical practice. The curriculum emphasizes the primary care needs of all patients and communities, particularly those in rural and underserved areas, while preparing students for practice in any medical or surgical specialty. Students learn to provide healthcare as members of interprofessional teams through an innovative curriculum that includes clinical problem-based learning and early clinical exposure.
Accredidation: The Accreditation Review Commission on Education for the Physician Assistant, Inc. (ARC-PA) has granted Accreditation-Continued status to the Pennsylvania State University Physician Assistant Program sponsored by Pennsylvania State University.

Description: The Intercollege Graduate Degree Program in Physiology provides an opportunity for students to study the functions of the human body and its component parts, from the molecular level to the whole organism. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in research and teaching in academia, industry, and government. ProgramName: Master of Science in Plant Biology
Requirements: Applicants must have an undergraduate degree in a biological, physical, or social science, and a junior/senior grade-point average of at least 3.00 (on a 4.00 scale). Required application materials include: official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, a statement of purpose, and a curriculum vitae or resume. For international students, TOEFL or IELTS scores are required. The Graduate Record Examination (GRE) is not required for admission.
Department: Huck Institutes of the Life Sciences / Graduate School
Description: The Plant Biology graduate program is an interdepartmental program that provides educational and research opportunities in fundamental plant biology from the molecular to the whole plant levels. Students and faculty in the program are studying the mechanisms of plant responses to the environment, the processes of plant growth and development, and the improvement of plants for the benefit of society. Because of the importance of plants to the health of the planet and to the humans who depend on them, research in plant biology is a high priority at Penn State. Students in our program have the opportunity to work with faculty from multiple departments in the Colleges of Agricultural Sciences, Engineering, and Science. The Plant Biology program offers both M.S. and Ph.D. degrees. Students have access to a wide variety of state-of-the-art facilities and equipment for research including one of the largest greenhouse complexes in the country, several field research stations, and a number of shared core facilities in the Huck Institutes of the Life Sciences. Current research within the program falls into four broad categories: cell and developmental biology; molecular biology and genetics; plant-environment interactions; and physiological and whole plant biology.

Requirements: Materials required for the application include: a completed online application and non-refundable application fee; a Statement of Purpose (stating your goals and why you wish to join the graduate program in Plant Pathology at Penn State); a Vita or résumé; three letters of recommendation (submitted through the online application system); and official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. Concentration: Public Budgeting and Financial Management, Homeland Security, Nonprofit Administration, and Public Sector Human Resources Management
Description: The Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.) program is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to serve as effective managers in public and nonprofit organizations. The curriculum is intended to prepare students for leadership roles in a variety of settings, including government at all levels, non-governmental organizations, and international agencies. The program emphasizes the development of core competencies in public management, policy analysis, and leadership, while allowing students to tailor their education to their specific interests and career goals. The M.P.A. degree is the recognized professional degree for careers in public service.
Accredidation: The M.P.A. program is fully accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA).

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Public Administration
Requirements: Admission Requirements: An earned master's degree from an accredited institution. Evidence of high academic achievement. Official Graduate Record Examination (GRE) scores are not required but may be submitted. Letters of Recommendation: three letters from people familiar with the applicant’s academic or professional work. Writing sample: an example of scholarly work (e.g., a master's thesis or a major research paper). Concentration: Public and nonprofit management, Public policy and analysis
Description: The Ph.D. in Public Administration is a research-oriented degree program that prepares students for careers in research, teaching, and advanced public management. Graduates are prepared for positions in universities, research organizations, and government agencies.

ProgramName: Master of Public Health
Requirements: Applicants must have a baccalaureate degree from an accredited institution. Applications must be submitted through the Schools of Public Health Application Service (SOPHAS). Required application materials include a current resume or curriculum vitae, a personal statement, three letters of recommendation, and official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. International students must also provide TOEFL or IELTS scores.
Concentration: Community and Behavioral Health; Epidemiology and Biostatistics; Health Policy and Administration
Description: The Master of Public Health (MPH) program at Penn State College of Medicine is a professional degree program for those who want to help people and their communities. Our mission is to prepare students to help improve the health of populations and to promote health equity through education, research and service. Students gain knowledge in core public health disciplines and develop specialized skills in their chosen track, which include Community and Behavioral Health, Epidemiology and Biostatistics, and Health Policy and Administration.
Accredidation: Accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH)

ProgramName: Master of Science in Public Health Sciences
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution. A minimum grade-point average of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) for the last two years of undergraduate study is required. Admission requires a completed Graduate School online application, nonrefundable application fee, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, and a 500- to 750-word personal statement (career goals and fit). International students must also submit TOEFL or IELTS scores.
Concentration: Community and Behavioral Health, Epidemiology, and Health Systems Research
Description: The M.S. degree is a research-oriented degree that focuses on the study of public health as it relates to health and medical research. This program is offered in the following specialty tracks: Community and Behavioral Health, Epidemiology, and Health Systems Research. The curriculum provides a strong foundation in the design and analysis of research studies, as well as the evaluation of health programs and policies. The program’s objective is to prepare students for research-based careers in public health, medicine, and related fields. Students will learn to apply quantitative and qualitative research methods to address public health challenges, conduct independent research, and effectively communicate research findings. The M.S. program is specifically designed to provide students with the skills and knowledge needed to pursue a doctoral degree or to work as a researcher in a variety of settings, including academic institutions, government agencies, and private industry.
Accredidation: The Penn State Public Health Program is fully accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health (CEPH).

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Public Health Sciences
Requirements: Applicants must have a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. Successful completion of a master’s degree in public health or a related field is preferred, but not required. A minimum undergraduate GPA of 3.0 (on a 4.0 scale) is expected. Standardized Test Scores: The GRE is not required for admission to this program. International applicants must provide proof of English proficiency (TOEFL or IELTS scores).
Concentration: community-engaged research, epidemiology and health systems research
Description: The Penn State College of Medicine is launching a new doctoral program in public health sciences. The program is designed to prepare the next generation of public health researchers to address some of society’s most pressing health issues, such as the opioid crisis, obesity and health disparities. The goal of the program is to prepare graduates for careers in research, teaching and service in academic, governmental and private sector settings. Students will learn how to design and conduct research to advance health at the individual, community and population levels.
Accredidation: The Department of Public Health Sciences is accredited by the Council on Education for Public Health

ProgramName: Master of Public Policy

Concentration: Criminal Justice, Data Analytics, Education Policy, Environmental Policy, Health Policy, International Policy, Labor and Employment Relations, and Social Policy
Description: The Master of Public Policy (M.P.P.) is a professional master’s degree designed for students who want to work as policy analysts, lobbyists, and policy-focused researchers in the public, private, and non-profit sectors. M.P.P. students will develop a skill set that includes policy analysis, program evaluation, management and leadership, and communication. Students in the program will also gain expertise in a specific policy area (e.g., health policy, data analytics, etc.).

ProgramName: Master of Professional Studies in Quality and Manufacturing Management
Requirements: For admission to the M.P.S. in QMM program, an applicant must hold a bachelor's degree in engineering, science, or another appropriate field from a regionally accredited institution (or a relevant international equivalent) with a grade-point average of 3.0 or higher (on a 4.0 scale) in the final two years of undergraduate study. Applicants should have at least two years of work experience in a manufacturing or service organization, although this may be waived for exceptional students. Applicants are required to submit: a completed Graduate School online application and payment of the nonrefundable application fee; a statement of purpose (1-2 pages) describing how the applicant’s professional and academic background has prepared them for the M.P.S. QMM program and how they plan to use the degree to further their career; three letters of recommendation from professional or academic references; and a current resume or curriculum vitae. GRE or GMAT scores are not required for admission.
Department: College of Engineering and the Smeal College of Business
Description:
The Master of Professional Studies (M.P.S.) in Quality and Manufacturing Management (QMM) is a 32-credit degree program. It is an online, interdisciplinary, professional master’s degree, provided by the College of Engineering and the Smeal College of Business. The QMM program provides an opportunity for students to study the fundamental principles of manufacturing and quality systems. Students learn to apply the technical and business skills needed to manage the design, production, and delivery of products and services. The M.P.S. degree is a unique combination of engineering and business topics, providing students with the skills and knowledge to lead the development of world-class, integrated manufacturing and service businesses. 

Educational Objectives:
1. The program graduates will lead the design, development, and improvement of manufacturing and service systems.
2. The program graduates will apply technical and business skills to evaluate and improve the quality of manufacturing and service processes.
3. The program graduates will evaluate manufacturing and service businesses as integrated systems of engineering and business functions.
4. The program graduates will utilize effective leadership and communication skills to work in multidisciplinary teams.

Student Learning Outcomes:
1. Communicate (in writing and orally) to a variety of audiences.
2. Work effectively in multidisciplinary teams.
3. Use technical and business skills to manage and improve manufacturing and service processes.
4. Analyze manufacturing and service businesses as integrated systems of engineering and business functions.
5. Explain and use the fundamental principles of manufacturing and quality systems.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management
Requirements: Requirements for admission to the Master of Science in Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management include: a minimum 3.0 grade-point average; an undergraduate degree in recreation, park and tourism management or a related field; a completed Graduate School application and fee; official transcripts; three letters of recommendation; a current resume or curriculum vitae; and a statement of purpose. International applicants must also submit TOEFL or IELTS scores. The GRE is not required for admission but will be considered as part of the application if submitted.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Description: The Master of Science (M.S.) in Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management (RPTM) program is designed to prepare students for research and teaching positions in colleges and universities or for advanced administrative positions in various recreation, park, and tourism settings. The program provides students with a well-rounded and sophisticated understanding of the field, while allowing for a specific focus that matches each individual student’s interests and goals. MS students work with their advisory committee to design a program of study that includes core RPTM courses, research methods and statistics, and courses in their area of interest.

ProgramName: Doctor of Philosophy in Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management
Requirements: Applicants for the Ph.D. in Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management must submit their application and supporting materials through the J. Jeffrey and Ann Marie Fox Graduate School. Required materials include: a current resume or curriculum vitae; a statement of purpose describing career goals and how the RPTM program fits those goals; three letters of recommendation from individuals familiar with your academic or professional work; a writing sample (e.g., a paper, article, or thesis) that demonstrates analytical and writing abilities; and official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended. Submitting GRE scores is optional but encouraged.
Department: College of Health and Human Development
Concentration: Human Dimensions of Natural Resources and the Environment (HDNRE); Clinical and Translational Sciences (CTS)
Description: The Ph.D. program in Recreation, Park, and Tourism Management (RPTM) at Penn State is designed to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to conduct independent research and to teach at the university level. The program emphasizes a strong foundation in theory and research methods, as well as the application of this knowledge to the field of recreation, park, and tourism management. Students work closely with faculty mentors to develop and conduct research projects that contribute to the body of knowledge in their area of interest. The program also provides opportunities for students to gain teaching experience through teaching assistantships and other instructional roles.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Rural Sociology
Requirements: To apply to the Rural Sociology Graduate Program, you must submit an application through the Penn State Graduate School. Application materials include: Penn State Graduate School Application and Application Fee; Transcripts; Three letters of recommendation; Statement of Purpose (professional goals and research interests); Professional Resume; Sample of your written work (class paper or publication); Official TOEFL or IELTS scores (if applicable). Description: The graduate program in Rural Sociology is one of the oldest and most distinguished in the nation. The faculty are international leaders in their fields, and our graduate students are among the best in the discipline. The program provides students with professional training in the application of sociological theory and research methods to address contemporary social problems in rural and urban areas, both domestically and internationally. Our alumni find careers in academia, government, and non-governmental organizations.

Description: The graduate program in Rural Sociology offers students an opportunity to explore the various problems and policies associated with changes in rural communities, natural resources, and the food system. The curriculum is designed to help students develop the sociological skills needed to analyze these changes and to provide leadership in addressing the challenges they present. The Ph.D. program is designed to provide students with advanced training in sociological theory, research methods, and the substantive areas of rural sociology. The program prepares students for careers in research, teaching, and professional practice in academic, governmental, and non-governmental settings.

Description: The Master of Engineering in Systems Engineering (SYSEN_MENG) is a non-thesis, professional master’s degree. The Master of Engineering in Systems Engineering program provides a broad foundation in systems engineering, including the ability to: provide a systems perspective on the design, development, and operation of products and services; analyze and model systems throughout the system life cycle; develop system architectures and verify/validate system performance; and apply systems engineering principles to a variety of applications.

ProgramName: Graduate Credit Certificate in Additive Manufacturing and Design
Requirements: Applicants must hold either (1) a baccalaureate degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution or (2) a tertiary (postsecondary) degree that is deemed comparable to a four-year bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited U.S. institution. This degree must be from an officially recognized degree-granting institution in the country in which it operates. Usually this is a degree in a relevant engineering, science or technology field. Admission to the certificate program also requires at least two (2) years of professional experience in an engineering or science field. International students must provide a TOEFL/IELTS score.
Description: The Graduate Certificate in Additive Manufacturing and Design program is designed to educate students and working engineers in the analytical and practical methods for the design and manufacturing of devices utilizing additive manufacturing. Additive manufacturing (AM) is a suite of emerging technologies that fabricate three-dimensional objects directly from digital models through the repeated addition of material. AM provides a new design paradigm, allowing for the creation of components with unprecedented levels of complexity and/or parts that are produced locally and on-demand. The program is designed to provide students with a foundational knowledge in the entire AM workflow, including the design, materials, and processing of AM parts. The program is a multidisciplinary program with faculty from the College of Engineering and the College of Earth and Mineral Sciences. As such, the program provides a unique opportunity to integrate various aspects of AM, including design, and the materials and processing of AM parts, to ensure students are provided with the most comprehensive AM education.

Requirements: To be considered for admission, you must have a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited institution. Applicants must submit a completed Graduate School application, official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, a current résumé, and a statement of purpose (one to two pages) that addresses your professional goals and why you are applying to the program.
Description: The 12-credit Graduate Certificate in Adult Basic Education is designed to provide professional development for practitioners who work in adult basic education (including literacy, numeracy, and GED preparation) and English Language Learning (ELL) settings. The courses focus on adult learning theory and its application to the adult basic education and ELL classroom, including teaching methods, curriculum development, and assessment.
